Hi Ben — great to meet you and Aisha on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can size the right Dedicated / quota profile: 

1) Current and expected volumes (please confirm):
   - Baseline: ~3M tokens/day (mostly prompts + completions for product search quality tests)
   - Peak/burst pattern: short bursts a few times per day up to ~25–50M tokens within 30–60 minute windows
   - Typical concurrency: ~150–250 requests/sec during peak minutes

2) Budget and unit economics:
   - Target cost band you mentioned: $X–$Y per 1M tokens — can you confirm a target $/1M tokens or a monthly budget range we should aim for?

3) Rate limits and overage tolerance:
   - We offer quota reservations with burst allowances and predictable overage pricing. For Dedicated customers we can set a soft quota with automated burst crediting and an overage rate that applies after soft burst exhaustion.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben/Aisha: confirm target $/1M tokens and any hard SLA on bursts (how critical is 0-drop traffic during a burst?)
- I'll share a short attachment with our recommended config options and a sample monthly pricing table for your estimated volumes.

Attaching: acme-consumption-estimates.xlsx (your consumption numbers + our suggested quota tiers) and redwood-overage-pricing.pdf (overview of burst/overage terms).

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming baseline: 3M tokens/day is correct for current pilot. We expect that to grow to ~8–10M tokens/day in production over the next 6 months.
- Bursts: the 25–50M tokens bursts happen mainly during promo blasts and peak shopping hours. During those windows we need best-effort low latency; dropping requests is acceptable for some non-critical flows but product search must remain high-quality.
- Budget: our procurement team is targeting ~$750–900 per 1M tokens as a target range for initial negotiations.

Questions: 
- How quickly can you increase quotas if we hit a burst beyond the reserved burst credits? We need to know typical lead time for quota increases and whether there is an automated path vs manual approvers.
- What's the incremental overage rate after we've consumed reserved quota + burst credits?

Thanks Ben — helpful context and the budget range is noted. To answer your questions: 

- Quota increases: we have two paths:
  1) Automated short-term burst credits: every customer gets a pool of burst credits (configurable) that absorb short spikes automatically with no manual intervention. These are intended for minute-to-hour bursts (what you described).
  2) Rapid quota increases: for sustained increases beyond burst credits we can provision additional quota within 24–48 hours for most standard requests; for very large capacity increases (e.g., consistent +100M tokens/day) we typically coordinate capacity planning and may require a short lead time depending on GPU availability.

- Overage rates: standard hosted overage is tiered. For Dedicated/Reserved customers we offer predictable overage pricing — example (for reference only):
  - Reserved quota exhausted -> soft bursts consume burst credits (no extra charge until credits exhausted)
  - After burst credits: overage charged at $1,200 per 1M tokens (can be negotiated to your target band for committed volume)
  - Committed monthly tier reductions available if you commit to a minimum monthly token spend (we can run scenarios based on your projected 8–10M/day).

Based on your $750–900 target, Rafael and I can run a committed example that hits that unit economics with a 6–12 month minimum commitment and slight uplift for guaranteed burst capacity. I'll loop Rafael to model committed pricing vs on-demand overage scenarios.

Confirming follow-up: Tue 2027-04-20 10:00 AM PT works; inviting Rafael to join.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Ben / Aisha — Rafael here from Sales Engineering. Thanks for the details — a few concrete items I promised to bring to the call today: 

1) Sample committed pricing (quick model):
   - No commit: baseline overage (after burst credits) $1,200 / 1M tokens
   - 6-month 500M/month commit: $900 / 1M tokens effective (meets top end of your range)
   - 12-month 1B/month commit: $750 / 1M tokens effective (hits your target)

2) Burst handling:
   - We provide a configurable burst credit pool sized to expected peak traffic. Credits auto-apply to bursts; once depleted, overage rates apply.
   - For product-search flows where drop is undesirable, we recommend a small dedicated reserved capacity buffer (hot pool) to keep latency stable during spikes — we can size that to keep 99th pct latency within your SLA.

3) Procurement & contract notes:
   - We can include a clause for expedited quota increases (24–48 hour SLA) for committed customers.
   - Overage terms can be capped/discounted under committed spend; we can add a monthly cap clause if you want predictable max spend.
